2012_033_032012regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of March 20, 2012, held at 6:00 PM at the Troy Center for Transition (GROW), 1291 Torpey, Troy, MI 48083 after Resolution 12-023 rescheduled it from March 6. It carries the agenda, minutes of the February 7 regular meeting and the February 14 special meeting and workshop, the January 2012 Treasurer's Report with a full check register, and two band-instrument bid items. Total disbursements in the period were $4,613,213.44, including $2,568,063.12 in checks; the business items rescind $3,036.00 awarded to National Educational Music Company and award the same clarinet to Midwest Musical Import for $5,520.00.
2012_033_032012regmtg.page:
**Meeting and agenda**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, March 20, 2012, 6:00 PM, Troy Center for Transition (GROW), 1291 Torpey, Troy, MI 48083; board offices at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Consent agenda (Item 5)**
A. minutes of the February 7, 2012 regular meeting; B. minutes of the February 14, 2012 special meeting; C. minutes of the February 14, 2012 workshop; D. Treasurer's Report - January 2012; E. bid for copy paper; F. bid for air filters; G. bid for utility vehicles.

**February 7, 2012 regular meeting actions**
Vice President Edmunds presided at 7:00 p.m., with President Philippart joining by teleconference from the FRN Conference in Washington, D.C. and about 24 audience members present. MSGCU's Bob Vincent presented mini-grants to teachers Marisa Contrera, Heidi Apol, Tonia Romancheck, Sherry Buczek and Gayle Spiteri. Dr. Fowler presented enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants at low, most likely and high levels. Resolution 12-019 closed Athens High School and Troy High School to open enrollment for 2012/2013, excepting not more than 30 ninth grade students from the Troy High attendance area. Resolution 12-021 awarded band uniforms to Stanbury Uniforms, Inc. for $113,629.44 ($118,364.00 less a 4% prepayment discount). Resolution 12-022 awarded instruments totaling $55,533.00 - $44,342.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund and $11,191.00 from the 2011-2012 General Fund. All roll calls carried 7-0; closed session on negotiations ran 8:15 to 8:35 p.m. under Public Act 267, Section 8(c). First readings were held of Board Policy B-1401, Minutes, and new Policy I-1701, Opting Out of Video Presentations, second reading set for April 17, 2012.

**Resolution 12-020 - amended 2011/2012 appropriations**

| Fund | Amended amount |
|---|---|
| General Fund | $130,078,102 |
| Special Revenue Funds | $8,372,374 |
| Debt Service Funds | $18,534,806 |
| Capital Projects Funds | $4,542,340 |
| Internal Service Fund | $116,000 |

**February 14, 2012 meetings**
A special meeting (6:00-6:05 p.m.) adopted Resolution 12-025 ratifying the January 25, 2012 tentative agreement with the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA) for July 1, 2012 through June 30, 2013, Ayes 7 Nays 0. A workshop (6:06-9:27 p.m.) covered middle school curriculum requirements and the Facilities Study Team report.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|

| Total - Special Revenue Funds | $39,899.30 |

| Total check disbursements | $2,568,063.12 |
| ACH debits | $35,264.96 |
| Outgoing wire transfers | $2,011,971.17 |
| Prior period void disbursements | $(2,085.81) |
| Total disbursements in period | $4,613,213.44 |

**January YTD budget report**
General Fund (101, 120, 122, 140) revenue of $127,175,517 budgeted against $59,026,239 actual, expenditures of $128,282,487 against $58,848,737, excess of revenue over expenditures (1,106,970), and fund balance moving from $18,803,870 at July 1, 2011 to $17,696,900 at June 30, 2012. Debt Service Funds 304/306/307 show property taxes of $19,402,035 budgeted and $12,128,271 collected, with redemption of principal of $12,460,000 still wholly unspent.

**Business items (03.20.12)**
Item 8.A rescinds the Bid 9723 award to National Educational Music Company for the Yamaha YCL-621 Low E Flat Base Clarinet in the amount of $3,036.00 after NEMC said it could not supply it at that price; NEMC retains the Gemeinhardt 462877 Piccolo at $417.00 from its $3,453.00 award. Item 8.B awards that clarinet to Midwest Musical Import for $5,520.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; bids were opened January 19, 2012 for Baker, Larson, Smith and Boulan Park Middle Schools and International Academy East, sent to 15 bidders with 11 responding, one a "No Bid".

**Identification.** Board of Education agenda packet for the Troy School District, Troy, Michigan, for the regular meeting of March 20, 2012 at 6:00 PM at the Troy Center for Transition (GROW), 1291 Torpey, Troy, MI 48083. Letterhead reads 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, web site www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. except July and August. Consent items: 5.A minutes of the February 7, 2012 meeting; 5.B minutes of the February 14, 2012 special meeting; 5.C minutes of the February 14, 2012 workshop; 5.D Treasurer's Report - January 2012; 5.E copy paper bid; 5.F air filters bid; 5.G utility vehicles bid.

**February 7, 2012 regular meeting minutes.** Called to order by Vice President Edmunds at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building with Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present and President Philippart participating remotely by teleconference from the FRN Conference in Washington, D.C.; Superintendent Fowler attended with administrators Birmingham, Keeling, Rajter and Machesky and approximately 24 members of the audience. Bob Vincent, Director of Sales and Business Development for Michigan Schools & Government Credit Union (MSGCU), presented cash-grant mini-grants to Marisa Contrera and Heidi Apol of Morse Elementary, Tonia Romancheck of Hamilton Elementary, and Sherry Buczek and Gayle Spiteri of Bemis Elementary. Resolution 12-018 approved minutes of the January 17, 2012 organizational meeting, the January 17, 2012 regular meeting and the January 27, 2012 retreat, 7-0.

Dr. Fowler presented enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Fred Ignatovich of Stanfred Consultants covering resident students, non-resident students, charter school students and schools of choice students at low, most likely and high levels. Resolution 12-019 closed Athens High School and Troy High School to open enrollment for 2012/2013 except for not more than 30 ninth grade students living in the Troy High attendance area, with siblings of Athens students in grades 9-11 allowed to open enroll; Dr. Machesky said a lottery would be used if applications exceeded 30. Resolution 12-020 amended the fiscal year 2011/2012 appropriations: General Fund $130,078,102; Special Revenue Funds $8,372,374; Debt Service Funds $18,534,806; Capital Projects Funds $4,542,340; Internal Service Fund $116,000. Resolution 12-021 awarded band uniforms to Stanbury Uniforms, Inc. for $113,629.44 ($118,364.00 less a 4% prepayment discount). Resolution 12-022 awarded instruments to Brook Mays Music $5,235.00, Interstate Music $1,065.00, National Education Music Co. $3,453.00, Sam Ash Music $10,264.00, Taylor Music $16,296.00 and Washington Music Center $8,029.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund, and Midwest Musical Imports $11,191.00 from the 2011-2012 General Fund; column totals $44,342.00, $11,191.00 and $55,533.00. Every roll call carried 7-0.

Robin Beltramini announced a Troy Youth Assistance "Dollars for Education" event and 2nd annual 50/50 raffle; Judy Armstrong-Hall spoke on common assessments and students writing versus typing. Resolution 12-023 rescheduled the March 6, 2012 meeting to March 20, 2012. First readings were conducted of revisions to Board Policy B-1401, Minutes (read by Mr. Hauff) and new Board Policy I-1701, Opting Out of Video Presentations (read by Mr. Schmidt), both reviewed by the Board's attorney for compliance with state law, the Open Meetings Act and the Revised School Code, second reading April 17, 2012. Athens student representative Jonny Dowdall reported $12,800 raised by the PTO's Lincoln Test Drive and Charity Week February 13-17 with a $24,000 goal; Mr. Hauff noted a Lukich's Restaurant fundraiser for the Athens orchestra February 29th, 3:00-8:00 p.m.; Dr. Fowler congratulated Alan MacNair on 25 years teaching in Troy. Resolution 12-024 took the Board into closed session on negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c) at 8:15 p.m.; it reconvened at 8:35 p.m. and adjourned at 8:36 p.m. Signed Todd Miletti, Secretary.

**February 14, 2012 meetings.** The special meeting opened at 6:00 p.m. under President Philippart with all seven members and administrators Fowler, Birmingham, Keeling, Machesky, Mull, Rajter and Witt. Resolution 12-025 ratified the tentative agreement reached January 25, 2012 between the Troy Board of Education and the Troy Educational Support Personnel Association/MEA/NEA (TESPA) for July 1, 2012 through June 30, 2013, Ayes 7 Nays 0; adjourned 6:05 p.m. The workshop opened at 6:06 p.m. at the Administration Building with Mrs. Jagels also present, plus Facilities Study Team members, Stu Redpath, Mike Zinn and about three other audience members, taking up recommended changes in middle school curriculum requirements and the Facilities Study Team report; adjourned 9:27 p.m.
